8750e52fb8b70a273de6e11d.title: Transfer news LIVE: Alvarez to Arsenal, Barcola bid, Fernandes talks
8750e52fb8b70a273de6e11d.author: Alex Young
8750e52fb8b70a273de6e11d.content:
![Add Evening Standard as a preferred source](https://www.standard.co.uk/img/google_preferred_source_badge_dark.png?quality=75&auto=webp&width=960) ![Bradley Barcola, Bruno Fernandes, Julian Alvarez]() The summer window is kicking into another gear as the likes of Arsenal, Manchester United, Chelsea, Liverpool and Tottenham work on deals to improve their squads before the start of the new Premier League season. The Gunners continue to be linked with Julian Alvarez and Victor Osimhen to bolster their attack, while Ezri Konsa and Jarrel Quansah continue to be of interest in defence. Man United are aware of interest in Bruno Guimaraes, amid reports of a £43million bid from Galatasaray, and are said to be interested in Adam Wharton and Kim Min-jae. Meanwhile, Liverpool have agreed personal terms with Ibrahim Mbaye as they take another huge step towards a double deal including Paris Saint-Germain star Bradley Barcola. Chelsea are braced for a Man City bid for Enzo Fernandez following Rodri’s move to Barcelona, while Pedro Neto has admirers in Saudi Arabia. Tottenham are closing in on the signing of Savinho and hope to then add Cody Gakpo to their forward line. Follow the latest transfer news, rumours and gossip live below! Latest transfer news and rumours Live updates Barcelona consider Viktor Gyokeres move Barcelona are interested in Arsenal striker Viktor Gyokeres if they fail to reach an agreement for Atletico Madrid forward Julian Alvarez. According to El Chiringuito, Atletico remain firm on their decision not to sell Alvarez, prompting Barcelona to explore alternative options. Gyokeres has only recently joined Arsenal but has already emerged as a potential target for the Catalan club should their pursuit of Alvarez collapse. Barcelona are reportedly preparing to make an approach for the Sweden international, with the situation expected to develop imminently. Newcastle still keen on £50m Lucas Bergvall Newcastle United remain interested in signing Tottenham midfielder Lucas Bergvall. According to the Daily Mail, Matthias Jaissle’s side are considering Bergvall as a potential replacement for former captain Bruno Guimaraes. The 20-year-old is regarded as one of Europe’s most promising young midfielders, but earlier this summer asked to leave after not being guaranteed regular first-team football. Tottenham are understood to value Bergvall at around £50m. Liverpool to submit new Bradley Barcola bid Liverpool are set to submit a fresh bid for Paris Saint-Germain winger Bradley Barcola as they close in on a deal for Ibrahim Mbaye. According to RMC Sport, a deal to sign Mbaye is progressing quickly after the player reached an agreement with Liverpool over a five-year contract. Liverpool are also deep in talks over Barcola, with a new bid expected this week. PSG want a potential club-record fee for the France star. ![](https://static.standard.co.uk/2026/08/18/12/01KZRTW82CCT9NK9YH60MGADZ1.jpg?quality=75&auto=webp&width=640) Atletico send Alvarez transfer message to Arsenal after 'Arteta talks' Julian Alvarez has been left out of Atletico Madrid's first La Liga game of the season, but the striker remains not for sale amid interest from Barcelona and Arsenal. The Argentine has been Barcelona's top transfer target all summer, with the player having repeatedly voiced his desire to move to the Camp Nou. Arsenal have long been interested in the former Manchester City forward, with Mikel Arteta reportedly driving the club's interest, but it is Barca were Alvarez wishes to go. Atletico have other ideas, and have repeated privately and publicly ruled out a summer exit for the striker. “It’s like when you go to court, that’s it, there’s nothing more to it. We’re looking after both the person and the player, and we understand that he is not in the right condition to play in this match." ![Julian Alvarez](https://static.standard.co.uk/2026/08/18/11/44/alvarez.jpeg?quality=75&auto=webp&width=640) Tottenham set Richarlison transfer stance Tottenham will demand a sizeable fee if they are to sell Richarlison before the close of the summer transfer window, writes Sam Tabuteau. There had been concerns that Spurs could lose the Brazilian striker, who is attracting interest from Everton, on the cheap with a year remaining on his current contract. But Standard Sport understands that Spurs retain the option to extend Richarlison’s contract by an extra 12 months, meaning they will not be forced into a cut-price sale. Spurs signed Richarlison from Everton in a deal worth around £60million in 2022. Richarlison finished last season as Spurs’ top goalscorer in all competitions, netting 11 times in the Premier League as the north London club narrowly avoided relegation. Despite playing a pivotal role in Spurs keeping their Premier League status, the 29-year-old continues to be linked with a move away. A return to his homeland, or former club Everton, have been mooted. ![

](https://static.standard.co.uk/2026/08/15/14/01M02V3KG7EVNXGMVVCAD3Z7V6.jpg?trim=0,0,226,0&quality=75&auto=webp&width=640) Man United, Newcastle and Tottenham monitor Edmond Tapsoba Manchester United, Newcastle United and Tottenham are monitoring Bayer Leverkusen defender Edmond Tapsoba. According to Fussballdaten, Leverkusen would be willing to discuss a deal for the 27-year-old centre-back at around €50m (£42.7m), despite his contract running until 2031. Tapsoba has been an important player for Leverkusen since joining from Vitória Guimarães in 2020 and has made more than 270 competitive appearances for the Bundesliga club. All three Premier League clubs are reportedly in contact with the Burkina Faso international’s representatives as they assess the possibility of a summer move. Chelsea demand £100m for Pedro Neto Chelsea are demanding a fee of £100m for Pedro Neto, Dom Smith reports. The Portuguese winger is attracting interest from Saudi Pro League club Al-Hilal, having also been linked with the likes of Manchester City, Tottenham and Liverpool this summer. However, Chelsea are not actively looking to sell Neto and would ask for an eye-watering £100m to entertain any prospect of a sale. Chelsea’s high valuation of Neto has been influenced by the inflated winger market elsewhere in Europe. Man Utd being new contract talks with Bruno Fernandes Manchester United have opened contract talks with Bruno Fernandes and insist he is not for sale at any price amid interest from Turkish giants Galatasaray, writes Sam Tabuteau. Standard Sport understands that United are determined to keep hold of their influential captain this summer and have held preliminary talks over a new deal. Fernandes’ current contract at Old Trafford expires next summer, but United, who have the option to extend it by a further 12 months, are relaxed about the situation and already in the process of negotiating fresh terms The Portuguese international enjoyed a stellar campaign last season as United qualified for the Champions League, breaking the single season assist record in the Premier League. Fernandes is viewed as a critical part of manager Michael Carrick’s plans. However, interest has begun to build in his services with clubs aware that he could leave on a free transfer next summer There was previously a £57million release clause in Fernandes’ contract, but that expired this summer and United have now made their stance on the former Sporting midfielder clear. ![

](https://static.standard.co.uk/2026/08/17/20/01M087ESDKKD461P1X06HMC9VS.jpg?quality=75&auto=webp&width=640) Official! Newcastle sign Amar Dedic Newcastle have signed defender Amar Dedic from Benfica in a deal worth around £30m. Dedic has signed a five-year deal to reunite with manager Matthias Jaissle, with whom he previously won the Austrian title at Red Bull Salzburg in 2023. "It's a special feeling and a really big honour for me to join Newcastle United," he said after the move was announced on Tuesday, his 24th birthday. "I'm really happy to be here and can't wait to start playing for the club and the amazing fans. "Working with Matthias again was a big factor for me. We know each other well. He knows what I can bring on the pitch and I'm really happy to be playing for him again. "Playing Premier League football at St James' Park is going to be really special. Every game feels like a big occasion, with an amazing atmosphere. I'm really excited to get started." Arsenal monitor Marc Pubill and attacking targets Arsenal remain keen to strengthen their defence and attack during the final days of the window. The Gunners made enquiries about Atletico Madrid defender Marc Pubill before the summer transfer window, but the Spanish club are equally determined to keep the 23-year-old. The Athletic report that left wing is Arsenal’s priority, though could move for a right-sided forward if the right opportunity becomes available. Kenan Yildiz and Julian Alvarez remain long-term targets, with Arsenal waiting to see if either becomes available before deciding whether to pursue alternative options.

Key developments include Liverpool pursuing Bradley Barcola and Ibrahim Mbaye, Barcelona targeting Julian Alvarez and Viktor Gyokeres, and Manchester United opening contract talks with Bruno Fernandes. Additionally, Newcastle United have completed the signing of defender Amar Dedic from Benfica for around £30 million.

Liverpool is progressing on a deal for Ibrahim Mbaye and preparing a fresh bid for Paris Saint-Germain winger Bradley Barcola.
Manchester United has opened contract talks with Bruno Fernandes and insists he is not for sale.
Newcastle United has officially signed defender Amar Dedic from Benfica on a five-year contract worth approximately £30 million.

820c33af2f9294ab00983655.title: Bizarre 'jellyfish spotted on Mars' in resurfaced Nasa images
820c33af2f9294ab00983655.author: Josh Milton
820c33af2f9294ab00983655.content:
![Side-by-side images show a tripod- shaped object on Mars.](https://metro.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/picture-nasa.png?w=646) 
When we think of Martians, we tend to think of little grey men.
But if a resurfaced image taken by a Nasa rover is anything to go by, the aliens that call Mars home are land-walking ‘jellyfish’. Maybe.
The photo was taken by Curiosity in August 2023, 3,924 Martian days, or Sols, into the extraterrestrial explorer’s time exploring the red planet.
The black-and-white panorama shows the 96-mile-wide Gale Crater, an ancient meteor impact crater, with a black, spindly object on the slopes.
Curiosity, a 1,000kg mobile laboratory sent to analyse Martian soil and rocks, frequently took photographs as it trundled around.
Strangely, the dark object was not there in a photograph taken less than 10 seconds before. It was also the final photo taken that day.

7e030d8bf7a5852ad7b60c91.title: Brits say ‘why have I got lurgy in summer’ as nation hit by wave of illness - AOL
7e030d8bf7a5852ad7b60c91.author: Ben Hurst
7e030d8bf7a5852ad7b60c91.content:
![Mirror UK](https://hermes.media.static.aol.com/logos/light/mirror-uk.png?v=1784567839)
![People in the UK are complaining of a wave of sickness like colds or flu - or even Covid - this summer](https://hermes.media.static.aol.com/media/2026/08/18/4c2195c6-f3c3-3123-9857-83f608f277bd/e2b63cea-fe4e-4c92-ab13-bb531f941d37.jpg)
People are complaining that a ‘summer lurgy’ is sweeping the UK - and fear there’s been a summer surge of Covid. People have taken to social media to complain of coughs, sniffles, sore throats and headaches - and wonder how it can happen in a heatwave.
Google Trends has reported that over the past week, “can you get the flu in summer?” is a ‘breakout’ term, signifying a growth of over 5,000% in search interest. The NHS is under pressure this summer with high attendances in A&E caused probably by the weather which has brought an increase in existing conditions worsening.
During the May and June 2026 heat events the UK Health Security Agency reported an estimated total of 2,877 heat-associated deaths - already near the highest levels ever recorded for a whole year. Respiratory conditions are known to be worstened by the heat.
Heatwaves also cause people to be more exposed as air conditioning and staying indoors to get out the heat can caused increase spreading.
In California and America reports suggest the summer peak of Covid-19 is in fact higher now than the winter. Dr. Erica Pan, director of the California Department of Public Health said: ““Anyone who hasn’t received a 2025-26 dose, or is due for the second dose, is encouraged to get vaccinated now, before the next COVID-19 surge,”
“Disease is on the rise in California, where we’re seeing increasing cases, increasing test positivity, increasing in our wastewater. This is a good time, actually, to protect yourselves or your family,” Pan told The Times in an interview, “because we anticipate, based on the last couple of years at least, that this may be the larger peak than the winter.”
On social media people complained at the cold surge. One said: ”I have that ‘summer flu’ that everybody’s going on about and I can confirm that it’s definitely Covid.” Another added: “how does someone get nasopharyngitis in the summer? how is this even possible!! i’m dying from the heat and now i have to deal with this inflammation and the flu?"
One speculated: “I’m suspecting we’re in the midst of a summer surge. A suspicious number of colleagues had headaches that went on for days. I’m getting over a ear infection and a relative has shingles.”
Frosty said: “I’m sick of having the flu in the middle of summer lol”. River added: “Currently under the weather and praying I don’t have the flu …. Summer sickness is the absolute worst! Have a good night folks it’s cold meds and sleep for me.”
A Londoner posted on social media: “Me and all my friends have gotten individually ill in the last week. Seems there is some gross summer cold travelling around at the moment. Haven’t left the house since last weekend, and seems my cold is just getting worse by each day!
“Feeling very sorry for myself, the heat is not helping, both in the sense of it’s too hot to be ill, and can’t go out in the cool mornings.”
Another added: “My team at work has had it this week, passed on at an event we attended.” Another person said: “Yes!!! Took out my entire family for a week!”
Dr Dominic Greenyer, a private doctor at the Health Suite, said: “Throughout the year, there are multiple viruses that come and go, and often, there can be clusters. So certain viruses may cause a cluster of cases, which we may be seeing at the moment in London. COVID is one of many viruses that circulate through the natural population every year.
“With these viruses, you can’t tell initially what it is because there’s a lot of crossover with symptoms. Most viruses cause symptoms such as muscle aches, high temperatures, and fever; these are just symptoms of feeling unwell. It’s hard to pin down a particular virus without getting tested but as most patients get better with no treatment, they don’t get tested. It’s usually only the patients who are very unwell and are admitted to the hospital who get tested.
“In 2020, we had a particularly severe strain that obviously caused a lot of health problems across the nation. However, is there something specific we should worry about with summer colds? No, not specifically. It could be viruses like COVID, among other things.
“General medical advice would be good self-care, get plenty of rest, fluids, a balanced diet, because all these things help the body to heal, regardless of what the cause is.”
Dr Greenyer also noted that most people tend to get better within 10-14 days and require ‘no intervention from medical services’. A pharmacist can give treatment advice and recommend flu remedies.
The NHS is urging millions of people to book their flu jab from today as the health service starts winter preparations earlier than ever.
As of yesterday (August 17), the national booking system is open so eligible people, including pregnant women and children, can pre-book their flu vaccinations when vaccinations start on September 1.
The NHS said it wants to do everything it can to ease winter demand after back-to-back heatwaves have seen staff treat record numbers this summer.
A&E attendances hit a record 2.5 million attendances in July – and staff experienced the 3 busiest months ever recorded between May and July in emergency departments.
Despite the record pressure, more patients were seen, treated or discharged within 4 hours than in June, with performance improving to 75.4%.
Flu season usually peaks in December and January, so the NHS is starting vaccinations in autumn, to ensure those at risk are protected and fewer people are hospitalised.
7e030d8bf7a5852ad7b60c91.summary: People across the UK are complaining of a summer wave of illness, including colds, flu-like symptoms, and fears of a Covid surge during recent heatwaves. Google Trends reported a massive spike in searches asking if people can get the flu in summer, while the NHS faces high A&E attendance pressures. Medical experts note that multiple viruses circulate year-round with overlapping symptoms, and recommend general self-care and rest since most people recover without medical intervention.
key_points: UK residents have taken to social media to report a wave of summer colds, headaches, sore throats, and suspected Covid cases.
Google Trends showed a breakout increase in searches for 'can you get the flu in summer?'
The NHS experienced high A&E attendances and record emergency department demand driven partly by worsening conditions during heatwaves.
Medical experts state that various circulating viruses share similar symptoms and most patients recover with self-care and rest within 10 to 14 days.
The NHS has opened early bookings for autumn flu vaccinations to help ease demand and protect vulnerable populations.
